title: Client Libraries Onramp — Notes & Scenarios (draft)
summary: Working notes for a lightweight, multi-language onramp for Redwood client libraries. Focus: minimal friction first-run, progressive disclosure of advanced features (streaming, functions, embedding workflows), and a reproducible playground for demos and tests.
objectives: Design a 5-minute first-run that highlights Redwood value (latency/streaming/compatibility)
Provide single-file examples for Python and TypeScript that can be copy-pasted into an editor
Create a CLI flow for local integration testing and mock-server demos
Outline three onboarding scenarios: prototype, integration, and eval
audience: Software engineers and ML engineers who are evaluating or beginning to integrate Redwood client libraries. Also useful for developer advocates writing workshops.
quickstart_outline: 0) Pre-req: sign up, get API key (or use local dev key from Redwood CLI)
1) Install package: pip install redwood-client OR npm install @redwood/inference
2) Set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-... (or use .env for local dev)
3) Minimal request: single Python script / single TypeScript file that does a generate call and prints output
4) Show streaming: same sample switched to stream mode (explain why streaming reduces perceived latency)
5) Show function/tool-calling stub: how to register a handler and parse structured output
6) Embeddings quick check: create an embedding for a short doc and run cosine-similarity with an inline snippet
7) Local mock server: spin up the Redwood CLI mock to test retries and timeouts without hitting prod
8) Next steps CTA: link to example app, SDK reference, and dedicated capacity docs
onboarding_scenarios: Prototype in 10 min: dev installs JS lib, runs single-file chat example against hosted model, forwards result to console and a small UI (React sandbox). Goal: see tokens->text in <2s for short prompts.

Integrate into backend: server-side example showing batching + request pinning, metrics to Prometheus, and fallback to smaller quantized model when latency spikes. Includes config snippet for rollout policy.

Eval loop: provide a test harness that runs a prompt suite, captures outputs, computes simple metrics (BLEU-ish, toxicity heuristics), and alerts when a regression exceeds threshold. Link to Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization/merging prompts.
playground_flow_notes: Keep the playground ephemeral: ephemeral API key via Redwood CLI, a lightweight React + Vite repo that hits /api/proxy which forwards to Redwood. Playground should default to a small curated model for cost control. Include a toggle to show raw token stream and a breadcrumb showing estimated token cost for the call.
code_snippets_examples:
PYTHON MINIMAL (copy-paste)

from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-small', prompt='Translate to French: Hello world')
print(resp.text)

TS MINIMAL (copy-paste)

import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'Summarize: Our weekly sync notes:' })
console.log(r.text)

STREAMING NOTE: show both callback and async iterator examples; explain backpressure and UI rendering considerations.
cli-first-run: redwood dev-mock --port 8080  # spin a mock server for offline testing
redwood inspect --model redwood-small  # print perf profile for the prompt size
observability_integration_tips: Instrument requests with a request-id header and expose per-request token counts to tracing
Expose per-model latency histogram and 99th percentile SLOs in the quickstart dashboard
Ship a sample Grafana dashboard JSON in the examples repo for immediate value
ux_principles: Minimal friction first: single-file examples that produce visible output without reading docs
Progressive disclosure: advanced features are optional and clearly labeled
Show the economics: inline token estimates and a 'what this call costs' helper
Failure stories are educational: show deterministic fallback examples (smaller model, cached response)
open_questions: Do we want to expose a 1-click ephemeral sandbox from the Console for the playground? (cost + security implications)
What should the default model be for quickstarts (redwood-small vs redwood-base)?
How opinionated should the client-side batching defaults be in the SDK vs left to the app?
Do we add a built-in sample prompts library or point to community examples?
next_actions: (Ava) Draft two single-file examples (Python + TS) and add them to client-libs/examples
(Liam) Prototype the CLI mock flow and document redwood dev-mock behavior
(Priya) Wire up a tiny React playground and measure perceived latency with streaming toggled
Schedule review with Developer Advocacy and Solutions Engineering for use-case validation
notes_to_self: This is intentionally rough. Keep iterations quick — users will learn from copy-paste examples more than long prose. Capture telemetry on which example gets run from quickstart so we can prune or promote examples.
